page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% for both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes. Single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip, and single-core Geekbench scores sit in the average tier. Conversely, multi-threaded operations, software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations show lower relative performance, placing in the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is highly constrained, with the medium 7B model achieving poor throughput under 11 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-standard-4 offers dedicated AMD EPYC hardware resources at a standard general-purpose density of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Because it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, it is best suited for workloads that do not require high-speed local disk I/O or parallel graphics processing. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, single-threaded application servers, basic text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments where single-core performance is prioritized over high multi-threaded throughput or massive memory bandwidth.
